kp7:1.2: and at the junctions and crossroads,
kp7:2.1: But when abundant food and drink,
kp7:2.2: both staple and non-staple, is prepared,
kp7:3.1: Thus those who are compassionate give to their (departed) relatives,
kp7:4.4: the departed relatives who have assembled
kp7:5.1: around the food and drink, respectfully offer their thanks:
kp7:5.4: Those to whom we owe this gain,
kp7:6.2: those who give are not without reward!”
kp7:6.3: For in that place there is no ploughing,
kp7:6.4: and cattle-rearing is not found there,
kp7:7.2: or buying and selling of gold.
kp7:7.3: The departed in that place who have died,
kp7:8.1: Just as water that rains on the highlands,
kp7:8.3: so too what has been given here
kp7:8.4: is of benefit to the departed.
kp7:9.1: Just as rivers that are full
kp7:9.3: so too what has been given here
kp7:9.4: is of benefit to the departed.
kp7:10.1: (Thinking): “He gave to me, he worked for me,
kp7:10.2: he was my relative, my friend, my companion,”
kp7:10.3: he should give gifts for the departed,
kp7:10.4: remembering what they have done before.
kp7:11.3: are of any use to the departed,
kp7:11.4: as long as their relatives continue (grieving) in this way.
kp7:12.1: But that gift that has been given,
kp7:12.2: and well placed in the Sangha,
kp7:12.3: is of benefit to them for a long time,
kp7:13.1: This then is the definition of a relative’s duties -
kp7:13.2: (and by this) great honour has been done to the departed,
kp7:13.3: strength has also been given to the monks,
kp7:13.4: and no little merit has been produced by you!
